title: SynerMedGen: Synergizing Medical Multimodal Understanding with Generation via Task Alignment
claim: Supervision aligned with the downstream generation task yields better representations than generic task supervision, improving both generation and understanding metrics.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: stacked ours/prior examples, paired data, two radar charts
description: The left panel has two stacked boxes. The top, orange 'Generation-aligned Understanding' box shows four tasks: CBCT/CT, CT-PET, CT/MRI and modality identification. Each task has medical image thumbnails and pink question bubbles with teal answers. The bottom, gray 'Tradition Understanding' box shows pathology, oral panoramic and fundus examples as generic captioning or QA. Vertical 'ALIGN' and 'MISALIGN' labels in the margin mark the contrast. The middle panel, 'Paired Cross-Modality Data', has four colored cards, each showing paired scans joined by bidirectional arrows (CT↔MRI, CBCT↔CT, MRI sequences, CT↔PET). The right panel has two radar charts. The top chart is labeled Gen. Perf. and shows SSIM across many synthesis tasks. The bottom chart is labeled Und. Perf. and shows accuracy. Each chart compares three settings: without understanding, traditional understanding, and generation-aligned understanding. The red generation-aligned polygon is largest in both charts.
caption: Overview of the comparison of the proposed generation-aligned understanding supervision and tradition understanding supervision. The right panel shows a comparison of SSIM values on the synthetic tasks under different understanding settings, as well as a comparison of accuracies on generation-aligned understanding tasks.
abstract: Unifying multimodal understanding and generation is a compelling frontier that is beginning to emerge in the medical field. However, the limited existing unified medical models typically treat understanding and generation as disjoint objectives, lacking a meaningful functional synergy. In this work, we identify and address a critical question in unified medical modeling: what form of understanding truly benefits generation. We present SynerMedGen, a unified framework built on the proposed principle of generation-aligned understanding, which synergizes understanding objectives with generation tasks via task alignment. SynerMedGen introduces three generation-aligned understanding tasks and a two-stage training strategy that transfers generation-beneficial representations learned during understanding training to medical image synthesis. Remarkably, even with understanding training alone, our SynerMedGen achieves strong zero-shot performance across 22 medical image synthesis tasks and demonstrates robust generalization to unseen datasets. When combined with generation training, SynerMedGen consistently outperforms state-of-the-art specialized medical image synthesis models as well as recent unified medical models. We also release a large-scale dataset named SynerMed consisting of 1M paired synthesis samples and 2M generation-derived understanding instances to support further research on understanding-generation synergy. Our project can be accessed at https://github.com/piooip/SynerMedGen.
